guide.description: ffmpeg reads a media file and writes a new one in whatever format the output filename's extension names — pick .mp3 and you get an mp3, pick .mp4 or .webm and you get a video, pick .aac and you get compressed audio. It's the tool you reach for first any time audio or video needs to change shape before it goes somewhere else. Flags like -b:a and -vf (covered in later lessons) can be combined with a format change in the same call.

flags.desc: the input media file to read

examples.note: the output extension picks the codec
